short_description: Therapeutic activities, direct (one-on-one) patient contact (use of dynamic activities to improve functional performance), each 15 minutes
lay_term: The provider uses various activities during direct contact with the patient to improve the patient’s functional performance. Use this code for each 15 minutes of activity. Explanation The provider uses activities such as bending, lifting, catching, and other everyday movements in direct, one on one contact with the patient. The provider chooses these activities to improve the functional performance of the patient, including physical mobility limitation, stability, strength, range of motion, and coordination. These activities involve movement and are important for medical rehabilitation. Therapeutic activities provide a number of benefits for patients. Providers may use these activities not only in the restoration of function but also in the maintenance and prevention of dysfunction at various ability levels. Report one unit for each 15 minutes. Terminology Functional performance: Level of achievement in routine activities, such as those related to specific tasks and goals, and requiring movement and use of multiple body systems. Therapeutic activities: Activities involving everyday tasks, such as bending, lifting, carrying, and squatting, to improve strength and range of motion. Read Less

short_description: Sensory integrative techniques to enhance sensory processing and promote adaptive responses to environmental demands, direct (one-on-one) patient contact, each 15 minutes
lay_term: In this procedure, the provider uses sensory integrative techniques in patients with established dysfunction of sensory processing, for example, children with autism, and brain injuries. This service helps to stimulate his or her sensory system and assist the brain to process information more effectively. Use one unit of this code for each 15 minutes the provider spends with the patient. Explanation Sensory integrative techniques are a treatment method in which the provider works with the patient who has an irregular reactivity to his or her sensory world. The provider works one on one with the patient to improve the way the brain processes and adapts to sensory information. The provider uses soft brushes, carpets, scooter boards, ramps, swings, and bounce pads to provide stimulation to the senses. He uses these tools to elicit a tactile sensation, or the sensation produced by pressure receptors in the skin, and then helps the patient learn how to process and respond to the stimuli. Use one unit of this code for each 15 minutes the provider spends with the patient. Terminology Sensory integration: It is a developmental process of arranging the sensory inputs so that brain produces a useful body response. Tips Read Less

short_description: Removal of devitalized tissue from wound(s), non-selective debridement, without anesthesia (eg, wet-to-moist dressings, enzymatic, abrasion, larval therapy), including topical application(s), wound assessment, and instruction(s) for ongoing care, per session
lay_term: The provider removes dead tissue from a wound without differentiating between viable and nonviable tissues. This service helps in assessing the depth of the wound, reduces the risk of infection and speeds the healing process. The service also aides in providing proper wound care instructions to the patient. The code is reported per debridement session. Explanation The provider uses one or more methods in a single session to remove dead wound tissue. After proper cleaning and evaluation of the wound, the provider may use a wet–to–dry dressing technique, where she applies saline gauze over the wound and allows the gauze to dry. Once the gauze adheres to the wound, the provider removes the gauze, thereby removing the dead tissue. Alternatively, she may apply naturally occurring proteolytic enzymes, like bacterial collagenase and papain/urea that selectively degrade the denatured collagen attached to the wound. The enzymes present no harm to the surrounding tissues, which is important for healing. Also, the provider may abrade the debris by scrubbing it vigorously or using a method such as larval therapy, sometimes referred to as therapeutic myiasis to treat skin and soft tissue wounds. In any technique, she then dresses the wound with non–adherent bacteria resistant gauze to prevent the wound from drying. The provider may treat one or more wounds during the session. She also instructs the patient or caregiver on how to provide care for the wound. Terminology Abrasion: Removal of superficial layers of skin. Collagenase: Enzymes responsible for breakdown of peptide bonds in collagen, a structural protein of connective tissues in animals. Denatured: Altering complex structure of protein without changing the basic arrangement. Devitalized tissue: Dead tissue appearing yellow, tan, or black in color; can be dry or wet. Larval therapy: Controlled method to treat skin and soft tissue wounds using live larvae or maggots, to remove dead tissue in the wounds; sometimes referred to as therapeutic myiasis. Non–selective debridement: Removal of dead tissues potentially along with nearby healthy tissues by methods such as wet–to–moist dressings, enzymatic techniques, and abrasion. Nonviable tissue: Tissue not able to live or develop independently. Papain: Enzyme derived from papaya; causes breakdown of proteins. Peptide: Small proteins having two or more amino acids. Proteolytic enzymes: Group of enzymes that breaks down proteins to peptides. Urea: Organic compound; product of protein metabolism. Viable tissue: Tissue able to develop and grow independently. Tips The intent of this code is to allow reporting by nonphysicians, such as physician assistants, nurse practitioners, wound care nurses, or physical therapists, who have licenses to perform the procedures involved in non–selective debridement. lay_term: The provider applies controlled subatmospheric pressure around the wound using durable medical equipment through a sealed dressing to remove fluids and infectious materials and to aid in healing of wounds that have a total surface area of less than or equal to 50 square centimeters. Explanation The provider cleans and checks the wound, with a total surface area less than or equal to 50 square centimeters, for absence of sinus tracts and fistulas. He then attaches a foam sponge, of the size and depth of the wound, over the wound using a transparent film. The film should be such that it provides a rigid seal. The provider; using appropriate durable medical equipment, then inserts suction tubing into the dressing through an opening in the transparent film and connects the tubing to a negative pressure therapy pump. He activates the pump. During the therapy, the provider observes the patient for signs of distress. He also ensures proper functioning of the equipment and the need to replace the canister where the suctioned material accumulates. He also instructs the patient or caregiver on how to provide care for the wound. Terminology Fistula: Abnormal connection between two organs inside the human body. Negative pressure: Lower pressure than the surrounding area. Negative pressure therapy system: Device for treatment of acute or chronic wounds by application of a vacuum using tubes, which carry negative pressure; a pump, which applies negative pressure; and a canister, which is an empty lidded cup that the suctioned material drains into. Sinus tracts: Tapered tunnels inside the body for fluids to escape. Subatmospheric pressure: Lower pressure than the atmospheric pressure. Tips After surgery, you may bill separately for negative pressure therapy as it is not a part of post–operative global care. Read Less

lay_term: The provider applies controlled subatmospheric pressure around a wound through a sealed dressing to remove fluids and infectious materials and to aid in healing of wounds that have a total surface area of less than or equal to 50 cm2. Providers may use this procedure to hasten the healing of decubitus ulcers, or pressure sores, as well as other slow healing or nonhealing wounds. Explanation The provider cleans and checks the wound, with a total surface area less than or equal to 50 cm2, for the presence or absence of sinus tracts and fistulas. If no sinus tracts or fistulas are present, he attaches a foam sponge, the size and depth of the wound, over the wound and covers it with a transparent film. He places the film so that it provides a tight seal. The provider then inserts disposable medical tubing into the dressing through an opening in the transparent film and connects the tubing to a negative pressure pump. He activates the pump. During the therapy, the provider observes the patient for signs of distress. He also ensures proper functioning of the equipment and whether he needs to replace the canister in which the suctioned material accumulates. He also instructs the patient or caregiver on how to provide continued care for the wound. Terminology cm2: Abbreviation for square centimeter, a metric unit of measure of area; the 2 is usually superscripted; 1 cm equals approximately 0.39 inches, or just over a third of an inch, so a square centimeter would be 1 cm x 1 cm; alternative sq cm. Fistula: Abnormal passageway between structures such as vessels, vessels and organs, or skin and organs or abdominal cavity. Negative pressure therapy system: A device for treatment of acute or chronic wounds that applies negative pressure, i.e., lower pressure than the surrounding area, to the wound to hasten healing; the system consists of vacuum tubes, a pump, and a collection canister. Sinus tract: Abnormal passage from an abscess in the body to the skin, typically the result of infection but may also develop in the joints of patients with rheumatoid arthritis; the tract may cause swelling and purulence. Subatmospheric pressure: Lower pressure than the atmospheric pressure, which is generally the pressure of the air around us and at sea level, designated as 1 atm; pressure decreases with increased elevation and increases with lower elevations, e.g. diving below the sea level. Tips For negative pressure wound therapy of a total surface area greater than 50 cm2, use code 97608. Read Less

short_description: Acupuncture, 1 or more needles; without electrical stimulation, initial 15 minutes of personal one-on-one contact with the patient Notes: (Do not report 97810 in conjunction with 97813)
lay_term: The provider uses solid, metallic, fine, single–use needles to pierce the skin and stimulate anatomical points on or in the skin by manipulating the needles by hand during an initial 15 minute treatment. This therapeutic intervention provides relief or prevention of pain, treatment of postoperative and chemotherapy nausea and vomiting, stroke rehabilitation, and treatment of asthma, addiction, and various other health conditions. Explanation The provider inserts one or more solid, metallic, hair–thin needles at critical points in the body that connect to nerves, muscles, and organs. The provider locates the insertion sites and then inserts and manually stimulates the needles. The provider may then leave the patient to rest. As treatment progresses, the provider checks on the patient and may readjust and manipulate the needles. The provider reports acupuncture based on 15–minute increments of face–to–face contact with the patient rather than being based on how long the acupuncture needles are in place. This code represents the initial 15 minutes of personal one–on–one contact with the patient. Tips A provider can report only one initial acupuncture code per patient per date of service as these codes include the complete initial service to identify the acupuncture needs of the patient including the patient evaluation, set–up, and treatment. You report acupuncture based on 15–minute increments of personal, face–to–face time with the patient and not the time the acupuncture needles are in place. Also, it is not appropriate to report 97810 or +97811, the nonelectrical stimulation codes, in addition to 97813 and +97814, the electrical stimulation codes, for the same 15–minute increment. Explanation The nonphysician qualified healthcare professional communicates with an established patient via online communication to address a health issue. The patient initiates the service using Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)–compliant, secure platforms. guidelines: Medicine Guidelines Range Specific Guideline Nonphysician qualified health care professional online digital assessment and management services are patient-initiated digital services that require patient evaluation and decision making to generate an assessment and subsequent management of the patient. These services are not for the nonevaluative electronic communication of test results, scheduling of appointments, or other communication that does not include assessment and management. While the patient's problem may be new, the patient is an established patient. Patients initiate these services through Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)-compliant, secure platforms, such as through the electronic health record (EHR) portal, email, or other digital applications, which allow digital communication. Nonphysician qualified health care professional online digital assessments are reported once for the nonphysician qualified health care professional's cumulative time devoted to the service during a seven-day period. The seven-day period begins with the personal review of the patient-generated inquiry. The cumulative service time includes review of the initial inquiry, review of patient records or data pertinent to assessment of the patient's problem, personal interaction with clinical staff focused on the patient's problem, development of management plans, including the generation of prescriptions or ordering of tests, and subsequent communication with the patient through online, telephone, email, or other digitally supported communication. All nonphysician qualified health care professionals in the same group practice who are involved in an online digital assessment contribute to the cumulative service time devoted to the patient's online digital assessment. The online digital assessments require visit documentation and permanent storage (electronic or hard copy) of the encounter. If the patient generates the initial online digital inquiry within seven days of a previous treatment or assessment and management service and both services relate to the same problem, or the online digital inquiry occurs within the postoperative period of a previously completed procedure, then the online digital assessment may not be reported separately. If the patient generates an initial online digital inquiry for a new problem within seven days of a previous service that addressed a different problem, then the online digital assessment is reported separately. If a separately reported evaluation service occurs within seven days of the initial review of the online digital assessment, codes 98970, 98971, 98972 may not be reported. If the patient presents a new, unrelated problem during the seven-day period of an online digital assessment, then the time spent assessing the additional problem is added to the cumulative service time of the online digital assessment for that seven-day period. (Do not report an assessment and management service within 7 days of reporting an online digital assessment and management treatment and/or service) (For an online digital E/M service provided by a physician or other qualified health care professional, see 99421, 99422, 99423)

guidelines: Medicine Guidelines Range Specific Guideline Nonphysician qualified health care professional online digital assessment and management services are patient-initiated digital services that require patient evaluation and decision making to generate an assessment and subsequent management of the patient. These services are not for the nonevaluative electronic communication of test results, scheduling of appointments, or other communication that does not include assessment and management. While the patient's problem may be new, the patient is an established patient. Patients initiate these services through Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)-compliant, secure platforms, such as through the electronic health record (EHR) portal, email, or other digital applications, which allow digital communication. Nonphysician qualified health care professional online digital assessments are reported once for the nonphysician qualified health care professional's cumulative time devoted to the service during a seven-day period. The seven-day period begins with the personal review of the patient-generated inquiry. The cumulative service time includes review of the initial inquiry, review of patient records or data pertinent to assessment of the patient's problem, personal interaction with clinical staff focused on the patient's problem, development of management plans, including the generation of prescriptions or ordering of tests, and subsequent communication with the patient through online, telephone, email, or other digitally supported communication. All nonphysician qualified health care professionals in the same group practice who are involved in an online digital assessment contribute to the cumulative service time devoted to the patient's online digital assessment. The online digital assessments require visit documentation and permanent storage (electronic or hard copy) of the encounter. If the patient generates the initial online digital inquiry within seven days of a previous treatment or assessment and management service and both services relate to the same problem, or the online digital inquiry occurs within the postoperative period of a previously completed procedure, then the online digital assessment may not be reported separately. If the patient generates an initial online digital inquiry for a new problem within seven days of a previous service that addressed a different problem, then the online digital assessment is reported separately. If a separately reported evaluation service occurs within seven days of the initial review of the online digital assessment, codes 98970, 98971, 98972 may not be reported. If the patient presents a new, unrelated problem during the seven-day period of an online digital assessment, then the time spent assessing the additional problem is added to the cumulative service time of the online digital assessment for that seven-day period. (Do not report an assessment and management service within 7 days of reporting an online digital assessment and management treatment and/or service) (For an online digital E/M service provided by a physician or other qualified health care professional, see 99421, 99422, 99423)

lay_term: The provider performs initial setup of equipment for remote therapeutic monitoring. The provider also educates the patient on use of the equipment. guidelines: Medicine Guidelines Range Specific Guideline Remote therapeutic monitoring services (eg, musculoskeletal system status, respiratory system status, cognitive behavioral therapy, therapy adherence, therapy response) represent the review and monitoring of data related to signs, symptoms, and functions of a therapeutic response. These data are reflective of therapeutic responses that provide a functionally integrative representation of patient status. To report 98975, 98976, 98977, 98978, the device used must be a medical device as defined by the FDA. Explanation After completing an initial 20 minutes of remote therapeutic monitoring (RTM) treatment management in a calendar month, a physician or other qualified healthcare professional completes an additional 20 minutes of treatment management. The total must include at least one interactive communication with the patient or caregiver. RTM is ordered by a physician or other qualified healthcare professional and involves using one or more devices for therapeutic data collection. The device must be a medical device as defined by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). RTM includes reviewing and monitoring data about signs, symptoms, and functions of the patient’s response to therapy to provide information about patient status. guidelines: Medicine Guidelines Range Specific Guideline Remote therapeutic monitoring treatment management services are provided when a physician or other qualified health care professional uses the results of remote therapeutic monitoring to manage a patient under a specific treatment plan. To report remote therapeutic monitoring, the service must be ordered by a physician or other qualified health care professional. To report 98980, 98981, any device used must be a medical device as defined by the FDA. Do not use 98980, 98981 for time that can be reported using codes for more specific monitoring services. Codes 98980, 98981 may be reported during the same service period as chronic care management services (99439, 99487, 99489, 99490, 99491), transitional care management services (99495, 99496), principal care management services (99424, 99425, 99426, 99427), behavioral health integration services (99484), psychotherapy services (90832-90853), health behavior assessment and intervention services (96156, 96158, 96159, 96160, 96161, 96164, 96165, 96167, 96168, 96170, 96171), and psychiatric collaborative care services (99492, 99493, 99494). However, time spent performing these services should remain separate and no time should be counted toward the required time for both services in a single month. Codes 98980, 98981 require at least one interactive communication with the patient or caregiver. The interactive communication contributes to the total time, but it does not need to represent the entire cumulative reported time of the treatment management service. short_description: Home visit for prenatal monitoring and assessment to include fetal heart rate, non-stress test, uterine monitoring, and gestational diabetes monitoring
lay_term: A home health provider, such as a registered nurse, typically visits a prenatal, or pregnant, patient with pregnancy complications to monitor the pregnancy and perform assessments to determine the health of the mother and fetus. The visit takes place in the patient’s home. Explanation The home health provider monitors the fetal heart rate through external monitoring, which is listening to the fetus’ heart with a special stethoscope. The provider may also conduct non stress tests or uterine activity monitoring, which monitor the fetus’ heart rate using two sensors that elastic belts hold in place, which are attached to the patient’s abdomen. One sensor uses ultrasound to measure the fetus’ heart rate, while the other measures movement of the fetus and can also measure contractions. The patient presses a button connected to the equipment when she feels the fetus move. The provider compares the heart rate during movement and at rest. The sensors are connected to equipment that records the results. The provider may also measure the patient’s sugar level to monitor gestational diabetes using a blood glucose meter that records the level of blood sugar. Read Less

short_description: Home visit for postnatal assessment and follow-up care
lay_term: A home health provider, such as a registered nurse, visits a patient and her newborn at home to review plans of care and provide additional resources to the patient. Explanation The home health provider assesses the health status of the patient and newborn. The visit may also include wound care for an episiotomy or C section, evaluation of medical equipment needs, education on breastfeeding and lactation, instructions on caring for the infant and how to recognize signs of illness, assessing the home environment for safety, and evaluating the infant for jaundice. The provider may also review plans of care for the patient and newborn. The provider educates the patient on required immunizations and schedules and additional services, such as parenting classes, and social services. She will also determine if the patient or newborn has any conditions that require a physician. Terminology Episiotomy: The provider incises the area between the anus and vagina to increase the size of the opening to allow for delivery of a newborn. Jaundice: Condition whereskin, mucous membranes, and sclera of the eyes turns a yellowish color, resulting from increased bilirubin in the blood. The liver produces bilirubin, a brown and yellow substance, when it breaks down old red blood cells. Read Less

When reporting a procedure with an unlisted code, submit a cover letter explaining the reason for choosing the unlisted code instead of a defined, active code.
